title: Multiplication of 3-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplication Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Multiply at least whole 3-digit by 2-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 multiplication worksheets: mental multiplication, grid method, 2-digit by 2-digit and 3-digit by 2-digit and word problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Multiply by the units, then by the tens, then add.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Break the numbers into hundreds, tens and units: 243 × 36 = 243 × 30 + 243 × 6.
  • Grid method: multiply each part and add the partial products.
  • In columns, multiply by the units, then by the tens (write a 0 first), then add.
  • Estimate: 243 × 36 is about 240 × 40 = 9 600.

Examples

Example

243 × 36

243 × 30 = 7 290

243 × 6 = 1 458

Answer: 8 748

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing the 0Multiplying by 3 tens gives tens.
Forgetting to carryAdd the carried digit.
Adding wronglyLine up the partial products.

items.q: What is 99 × 7?
What is 2 × 36 × 5?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 2 × 5 = 10, then 10 × 36 = 360. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: Multiply by 10, then halve, to find 46 × 5.
items.e: × 5 is the same as × 10, then halve. 46 × 10 = 460. Half of 460 = 230.

items.q: What is 60 × 7?
items.e: 60 is 6 tens. 6 × 7 = 42, so 6 tens × 7 = 42 tens = 420.

items.q: Double, then double again, to find 37 × 4.
items.e: × 4 is double, double. Double 37 = 74. Double 74 = 148. Doubling only once gives 74; three times gives 296.

items.q: What is 19 × 6? (Hint: 19 is 1 less than 20.)

items.e: 24 is one less than 25, so take away one 8: 200 − 8 = 192.

items.q: What is 25 × 4 × 9?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. 25 × 4 = 100, then 100 × 9 = 900. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: What is 5 × 17 × 2?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 5 × 2 = 10, then 10 × 17 = 170. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.
24 is double 12, so 24 × 7 is double 84 = 168.

items.q: What is 400 × 6?
items.e: 400 is 4 hundreds. 4 × 6 = 24, so 4 hundreds × 6 = 24 hundreds = 2 400.

items.q: What is 900 × 8?
items.e: 900 is 9 hundreds. 9 × 8 = 72, so 9 hundreds × 8 = 72 hundreds = 7 200.

items.q: What is 18 × 50?
items.e: × 50 is the same as × 100, then halve. 18 × 100 = 1 800. Half of 1 800 = 900.

items.q: What is 4 × 19 × 25?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 4 × 25 = 100, then 100 × 19 = 1 900. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: What is 16 × 25? (Hint: halve one number and double the other.)
items.e: Halve 16 and double 25: 16 × 25 = 8 × 50 = 4 × 100 = 400. If you double one number you must halve the other.

What is 34 × 10?
items.e: × 10 moves every digit one place to the left: 34 ones become 34 tens. Write a 0 in the ones place: 34 × 10 = 340.

items.q: What is 715 × 100?
items.e: × 100 moves every digit two places to the left: 715 ones become 715 hundreds. Write two zeros: 715 × 100 = 71 500.

items.q: What number goes in the part marked ?
items.e: The ? part is 7 wide and 2 tall: 7 × 2 = 14. All four parts add to 67 × 42 = 2 814.

items.q: Which parts add up to 59 × 57?
items.e: Each part of one number multiplies each part of the other, so there are 4 parts. Partition 59 = 50 + 9 and 57 = 50 + 7. 50 × 50 = 2 500, 9 × 50 = 450, 50 × 7 = 350, 9 × 7 = 63. Add: 2 500 + 450 + 350 + 63 = 3 363.

items.e: Partition 55 into 50 + 5. Both parts must be multiplied by 9: 50 × 9 + 5 × 9 = 450 + 45 = 495.

items.e: Each part of one number multiplies each part of the other, so there are 4 parts. Partition 27 = 20 + 7 and 64 = 60 + 4. 20 × 60 = 1 200, 7 × 60 = 420, 20 × 4 = 80, 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 1 200 + 420 + 80 + 28 = 1 728.

items.q: Calculate 95 × 69
Which calculation gives the first row, 294?
items.e: The first row multiplies all of 98 by the ones digit, 3: 98 × 3 = 294. Then the second row is 98 × 80 = 7 840.

items.e: Row 1 should be 552, not 542: 2 × 6 = 12, write 2, exchange 1; 9 × 6 + 1 = 55, write 55. The exchanged digits were not added. The correct answer is 8 832.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 67 × 48?
items.e: Round 67 to the nearest ten: 70 (the next digit is 7, so round up). Round 48 to the nearest ten: 50 (round up). 70 × 50 = 3 500. The exact answer is 3 216, close to 3 500.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 386 × 42?
items.e: Round 386 to the nearest hundred: 400 (the next digit is 8, so round up). Round 42 to the nearest ten: 40 (round down). 400 × 40 = 16 000. The exact answer is 16 212, close to 16 000.

What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 365 × 60. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 365 × 6: 5 × 6 = 30, write 0, regroup 3; 6 × 6 + 3 = 39, write 9, regroup 3; 3 × 6 + 3 = 21, write 21. The row is 21 900, not 2 190. Check: 3 285 + 21 900 = 25 185.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
A family uses 165 litres of water a day. How much water do they use in a week?
items.e: Equal groups: 7 days × 165 litres, so multiply 165 × 7. Ones: 5 × 7 = 35. Write 5, exchange 3. Tens: 6 × 7 + 3 = 45. Write 5, exchange 4. Hundreds: 1 × 7 + 4 = 11. Write 11. Answer: 1 155.

items.q: A box holds 144 pencils. The school office orders 23 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 23 boxes × 144 pencils, so multiply 144 × 23. Row 1: 144 × 3 = 432. Row 2: 144 × 20 = 2 880 (write the place-holder 0, then 144 × 2 = 288). Add: 432 + 2 880 = 3 312.

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 175 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 12 people?
items.e: 12 people is 3 times as many as 4 people (4 × 3 = 12), so use 3 times as much flour: 175 × 3 = 525 g. Do not multiply by 12: the recipe is for 4 people, not 1.

items.q: A bakery bakes 2 350 bread rolls every day. How many rolls does it bake in 6 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 6 days × 2 350 rolls, so multiply 2 350 × 6. Ones: 0 × 6 = 0. Write 0. Tens: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3. Hundreds: 3 × 6 + 3 = 21. Write 1, exchange 2. Thousands: 2 × 6 + 2 = 14. Write 14. Answer: 14 100.

items.q: Palesa says 286 × 34 = 2 002. Estimate to check. Is her answer sensible?
items.e: 286 rounds to 300 and 34 rounds to 30. 300 × 30 = 9 000. 2 002 is far from 9 000, so it cannot be right. Palesa forgot the place-holder 0 in the second row. The correct answer is 9 724.

items.q: The school hall has 27 rows of chairs with 18 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
items.e: Equal groups: 27 rows × 18 chairs, so multiply 27 × 18. Row 1: 27 × 8 = 216. Row 2: 27 × 10 = 270 (write the place-holder 0, then 27 × 1 = 27). Add: 216 + 270 = 486.

items.q: A dripping tap wastes 45 mℓ of water every hour. How much water does it waste in 24 hours?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 hours × 45 mℓ, so multiply 45 × 24. Row 1: 45 × 4 = 180. Row 2: 45 × 20 = 900 (write the place-holder 0, then 45 × 2 = 90). Add: 180 + 900 = 1 080.

items.q: A rabbit has a mass of 2 400 g. A guinea pig is 14 as heavy. What is the mass of the guinea pig?
items.e: “14 as heavy” means divide into 4 equal parts: 2 400 ÷ 4 = 600 g. Multiplying by 4 gives 9 600 g, which is heavier, not lighter.

items.q: A glass holds 250 mℓ. A jug holds 6 times as much. How much does the jug hold?
items.e: 6 times as much, so 250 mℓ × 6: 250 × 6. Ones: 0 × 6 = 0. Write 0. Tens: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3. Hundreds: 2 × 6 + 3 = 15. Write 15. Answer: 1 500.

items.q: A lorry carries 32 crates. Each crate has a mass of 145 kg. What is the total mass of the crates?
items.e: Equal groups: 32 crates × 145 kg, so multiply 145 × 32. Row 1: 145 × 2 = 290. Row 2: 145 × 30 = 4 350 (write the place-holder 0, then 145 × 3 = 435). Add: 290 + 4 350 = 4 640.

items.q: A SkyTrain carries 145 riders on one trip. How many riders does it carry on 8 trips?
items.e: 8 trips × 145 riders, so multiply 145 × 8. 5 × 8 = 40, write 0, regroup 4; 4 × 8 + 4 = 36, write 6, regroup 3; 1 × 8 + 3 = 11, write 11. Answer: 1 160 riders.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 86 × 29?
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten. 86 has 6 ones, so it rounds up to 90. 29 has 9 ones, so it rounds up to 30. 90 × 30 = 2 700 (tens × tens = hundreds). The exact answer is 2 494, close to 2 700.

items.q: Priya works out 72 × 39 = 2 808. Estimate to check. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 72 × 39 is about 70 × 40 = 2 800. 2 808 is close to 2 800, so the answer is reasonable.

items.q: Liam practises the piano for 35 minutes a day. How many minutes does he practise in 28 days?
items.e: 28 days × 35 minutes, so multiply 35 × 28. Row 1: 35 × 8 = 280. Row 2: 35 × 20 = 700 (write the placeholder 0, then 35 × 2 = 70). Add: 280 + 700 = 980.

items.q: Volunteers plant cedar seedlings in 37 rows, with 24 seedlings in each row. How many seedlings do they plant?
items.e: 37 rows × 24 seedlings, so multiply 24 × 37. Row 1: 24 × 7 = 168. Row 2: 24 × 30 = 720 (write the placeholder 0, then 24 × 3 = 72). Add: 168 + 720 = 888.

items.q: Each shelf in the school library holds 128 books. How many books fit on 7 shelves?
items.e: 7 shelves × 128 books, so multiply 128 × 7. 8 × 7 = 56, write 6, regroup 5; 2 × 7 + 5 = 19, write 9, regroup 1; 1 × 7 + 1 = 8, write 8. Answer: 896 books.

items.e: Estimate: 58 × 34 is about 60 × 30 = 1 800. 406 is far from 1 800, so it cannot be right. Elna forgot the placeholder 0 in the tens row. The correct answer is 1 972.
